doc.title: John Fedchock interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 28, 2015

chapter: Early training and path to Woody Herman
title: Eighth grade, loving the trombone and transcribing Tommy Dorsey
summary: An uncle's Tommy Dorsey double album led to early attempts at transcribing and writing.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Yeah. Okay. Well when you were in eighth grade, I’m just going to pick eighth grade —
Because it’s an interesting time for a young man. Did you have these aspirations then?

I loved music and I loved the trombone and I loved just the social aspect of the band, but I also loved the fact that it was something that I did pretty well and I felt like it was something that would get me out of my shell a little bit. And I started messing around with writing a little bit. I had — my uncle sent me a double album set of Tommy Dorsey’s big band. He said if you play trombone you should know who Tommy Dorsey is. So I listened to that, and tried to transcribe one of the charts, and this was in eighth grade. You know I didn’t really know what I was doing. And I’m trying to transcribe it

off an LP. So you can imagine what it did to the record. But that was a learning experience. And then — so it kind of started around that time believe it or not, like seventh or eighth grade where I was thinking this is a lot of fun, I wish I could do this all the time. I didn’t know you could actually do it, but I was hoping that there was some way I could continue playing that kind of music.
